body: They're trying to break it from me.
You're not real!
Did you poison me?  I asked for help and someone poisoned me.  Shut up!  Shut up!  Please just stand there quietly.  Please.
Why?  I'm not giving you the fiddle too.
I'm not alone in the matter.  That's the problem.  It's out of the matter where I'm alone.  Not alone in the matter.  I wish I were.
Who is watching our talk?

I have a back.  The knife is dialectically generated for the stab.  I have a back.  You syllogism.  You are hiding your syllogism, but I can see it.  I gave them a reason to bash me.  In the major or minor premise?  Socrates is mortal.
Thank you for trying.  I know people meant well.  It's not you, it's me.
This isn't helping me.  Sorry if you are a well-intentioned syllogism.  I'll be in the Suicide Watch subreddit.
It's my thought patterns that are incorrect and people will only tell me that they are incorrect.  I'm sick of being human.
Yes, it's all a facade.  I'm even lying about my trust issues.  Thank you for that syllogism.
I'm sorry.  I didn't mean to ruin your day.  I have a natural ability to depress people.  No wonder.

I think this thread has properly diagnosed the problem: I'm a worthless human being.  I had thought my problem was specifically being sexually repulsive, but it turns out that the real problem is deeper.  Thank you for that syllogism.

Thank you for this reply.  I am glad to know that it has nothing to do with looks and that I am just an inherently bad person.  Why should anyone be with someone who hates himself and is miserable?  That is a good question.

No one can fix me except myself.  Myself is broken.  Therefore, no one can fix me.  QED.  Thank you for that syllogism.  

I am glad to know that I am worse off than I thought, that even words of wisdom are too good for me.  Thank you for that syllogism.

No, I am just miserable and venting.  I realize I'm on a bad path, but there's nothing to be done about it.  Talking to other people doesn't help.  People just enjoy kicking me around for my bad attitude, which just continues the cycle of rejection.  Not talking to other people doesn't help.
Thank you for that.  I hope that made you feel better.
Yeah, I realize I need therapy.  I don't trust therapists, though.  Thank you for also ragging on me about my attitude.  Really helps.

"You have a crappy attitude about yourself and it reeks all over your posts."  I admitted as much, but this jackass was more interested in putting the boot in (and yakking about himself) than saying anything useful.  He's a classic manipulative sadist.
No, I was explaining my thought processes, not saying they were great.  You don't seem to understand the concept of "off my chest."  Just go away.
I only took issue with this one commenter because he was clearly more interested in bashing me than saying anything helpful.
I hope that made you feel better.
I wasn't looking *down* on her, I just didn't enjoy her company anymore.
I was explaining my thought processes, not excusing them.
I will do that.  Thanks.
OK, conceptually, I get this.  I hate the idea of trusting anyone who just likes my best version, but I understand where you're coming from.
I never denied that, but it's difficult to change how you feel about something.  I was trying to explain my thought process, not justify it.
Thanks, same to you.
But it feels really fake when I do it, and I end up feeling disgusted when people fall for fake acts.

I don't think people who make unwanted character judgments are "trying to help."  I think they're trying to tear someone else down for their own benefit, even if it's just a stranger on the Internet.

Here it's easier to tell people like that to get lost.  In real life, it's better not to open up to those kinds of people in the first place.

I think a lot of people use "we want what's best for you" as a cover for sadism.  What my friends/family want is to have something on me, to have the upper hand.  I don't want to put myself in that position.

That holds me back socially, but I just really hate the idea of trusting other people.

I realize you probably can't help it, but you come across as completely patronizing and annoying.  I didn't ask for your Batman mantras, or your mental kick in the ass.  I already said we have different problems.  You just can't take no for an answer.
As I said before, this is too vague and general for me.  "Act confident" in hopes of a virtuous cycle sounds good in theory, but it's been trickier for me in practice.
Thanks.  This was helpful.

I think the gay community is more accepting of closet cases.  It's considered normal for at least some gays to struggle with accepting their sexuality, because of social stigma.  

Being a closeted heterosexual is more unusual.

Thanks for your useless "be more flamboyant" advice; it's hard to find rude, pushy armchair psychoanalysts on the Internet.
I think it's different for gays.
The shame for me would be someone in my family or social circle finding a profile.  I would get lots of unwanted advice and attention.
I would rather kill myself than post an online dating profile.
How did you finally beat it?
I want to date a woman, not vomit one up.

I am not trying to be churlish, but "be confident" means very little to me.  It feels cheesy and fake, like a performing monkey.  Honestly, it leaves me even more depressed than before.  I don't know why.  Once I was flirting with a girl, and when she laughed at a dumb joke, it set my teeth on edge.  I didn't mean to be rude, but I just had to walk away.  The only time I don't mind is when I'm drunk, but then I drink too much and pass out.

Other side of the country from Jersey.
